subject: Reserved capacity allocation decision matrix & escalation path for NovaHealth pilot
body:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@novahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask for NovaHealth pilot

Jonas / Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move the pilot to a reserved capacity model, but procurement needs clarity on two things before we sign:

1) A simple mapping between committed capacity (vGPU-hours) and the discount we get today.
2) Protection if GPU market prices spike mid-term — we need either an indexation clause or an equivalent credit mechanism.

We're planning a 9-month pilot with potential to scale into a multi-year commitment. Can you share an example decision matrix and the approval path if we ask for a price protection clause?

Best,
Rajiv
Sr. Platform Ops, NovaHealth

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@novahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:05:21 -0700
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity ask for NovaHealth pilot

Rajiv —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is commit_matrix_v2.xlsx that lays out our recommended guardrails. High level:

- Commit tiers (monthly vGPU-hour buckets): 10k / 25k / 75k / 200k
- Baseline discount vs on-demand: 8% / 14% / 22% / 30% respectively
- Escalator: finance-triggered approval for discounts > 20% (requires VP-Fin sign-off)
- Price protection options (pick one):
  a) GPU-indexation: our per-token price ties to a GPU index; if index rises >15% YoY, provide a rebate covering delta beyond 15% up to an agreed cap.
  b) Fixed rebate pool: a capped credit pool paid quarterly if realized infrastructure cost per token increases by >10%.

Operational notes:
- Canary pool: we propose reserving a small dedicated canary pool (5% of committed capacity) on a separate SKU to handle early surge and allow incremental scaling without reprovisioning the whole reserved fleet.
- Reconciliation: monthly usage reconciliation with 30-day invoice adjustments.

Internal approvals:
- Pricing up to 20% discount: Sales lead + Finance SA review.
- Discount >20% or rebate/escrow arrangements: VP-Finance + Legal must sign off.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm which price protection option NovaHealth prefers (indexation vs rebate).
2) Agree on commit tier and canary allocation.
3) Send final language request so Legal can draft amendment (I attached related Drive link).

I will loop in Grace (Finance) and Laura for the formal approval path.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: commit_matrix_v2.xlsx (matrix, assumptions tab)

---

On Sun, 1 Nov 2026 08:22:15 -0700, laura_bennett@redwood.com wrote:
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@novahealth.com>
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask for NovaHealth pilot

Team —

Thanks Jonas and Rajiv. A few finance items we need clarified before we'll sign off on any rebate or indexation approach: 

1) Minimum Revenue Guarantee (MRG): do they want a true MRG (non-refundable) or a flexible commit with an overage reconciliation? The economics differ.
2) Breakpoint mechanics: for example, if NovaHealth hits 60% of the next tier for three consecutive months, do we auto-upgrade capacity or do they pay a retroactive true-up?
3) Escrow/credit cap: if we accept indexation, propose we cap liability at 12% of ARR for the first year. Anything beyond that requires executive approval.

I've sketched a sensitivity table and attached pricing_sensitivity_table.csv — shows net blended margin across a range of GPU price moves (±30%). The key callouts:
- At >+20% GPU cost shock, our margin at the 30% discount tier compresses below acceptable thresholds unless we use a capped rebate structure.
- Short-term pricing protection is manageable with a rebate pool; long-term indexation without hard caps exposes us to tail risk.

My suggestion for NovaHealth pilot: offer a 9-month commit at the 22% discount (75k tier) with:
- A 10% up-front prepay discount (applied to quarter 1).
- A quarterly reconciliation with a capped rebate triggered only if GPU index > +15% (cap = 10% of annualized committed fees).

If NovaHealth accepts that, escalation only needed for rebate cap increases or if they demand MRG instead of flexible commit.

Laura Bennett
Head, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing_sensitivity_table.csv

---

On Mon, 2 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800, jonas_weber@redwood.com wrote:
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@novahealth.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Subject: Finalize approval path and draft amendment request — NovaHealth

Laura / Grace —

Thanks for the analysis and the sensitivity table. To keep the deal moving and avoid a protracted negotiation on open caps, here's the proposed commercial offer we will present to NovaHealth: 

- Term: 9 months pilot, auto-convert to 12-month rolling if utilization >80% of committed capacity for 2 consecutive months.
- Tier: 75k vGPU-hour monthly (22% discount) with a 5% canary pool reserved on a different SKU.
- Up-front: 10% prepay discount applied to initial invoice.
- Price protection: GPU-indexed rebate if index > +15% YoY, rebate cap = 10% of annualized committed fees.
- Approval: Sales lead + Laura for present offer. If NovaHealth asks to increase rebate cap beyond 10% or to convert to a non-refundable MRG, route to VP-Fin (Tim Harper) and Legal. Discounts >25% require VP-Sales approval.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Legal: draft short amendment language mapping indexation calculation and rebate mechanics (Jonas -> Legal, request by 2026-11-05).
- Finance: confirm cashflow treatment for the 10% prepay and rebate cap (Grace -> 2026-11-04).
- Sales: present commercial term to NovaHealth procurement and capture written confirmation on choice of price protection (Jonas -> 2026-11-03).

Rajiv — if this aligns with procurement's tolerance, let us know and I'll put the formal offer in HubSpot and ping Legal to get an amendment started. If you prefer the fixed rebate pool instead of indexation, say so and we'll surface the calculations.

Thanks all,
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal_amendment_draft_notes.pdf
